subject: Cross-cloud marketplace syndication & SKU playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, vanessa.ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa.cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@aws-partner.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@azurepartners.com>, Sophie Leclerc <sophie.leclerc@gcp-marketplace.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-cloud marketplace syndication & SKU playbook

Team —

I pulled together an initial matrix for how we could syndicate product SKUs and packaging across AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplaces. The goal: a single playbook we can operationalize with each partner for listing cadence, SKU granularity, and region coverage. Key ask: get alignment on which SKUs to list where (Starter / Scale / Enterprise), region priorities, and who will own co-sell/beachheads per cloud.

Attached: syndication_matrix_v0.3.xlsx (working draft), co-sell_contacts.csv, pricing_tiers_draft.pdf

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- AWS: full three-tier SKU (Starter/Scale/Enterprise) — prioritize US/EU first, then AUS/IN as wave 2. AWS co-sell team wants multiple SKUs to map to their SaaS contract SKUs.
- Azure: consolidate Starter+Scale into a single "Growth" SKU for simpler procurement in enterprise accounts, list in US/EU only initially.
- GCP: list Starter as free/trial offering + Enterprise; delays expected for lengthy onboarding. Recommend targeted regions (US, GCP EU-west).

Open questions:
1) Do we standardize SKU names or rely on cloud-specific packaging?
2) How strict do we need to be on region parity vs. speed-to-market?
3) Who signs off on pricing band differences per cloud (sales/finance/legal)?

Please reply with: acceptance/comment suggestions, and call out any blockers by EOD. Maya/Tom/Sophie, if you can confirm partner-specific constraints (e.g., SKU naming rules, minimum listing metadata), that would be great.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Marketplace Partnerships (acting)
Redwood Inference
(attachment: syndication_matrix_v0.3.xlsx)
(attachment: co-sell_contacts.csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, vanessa.ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa.cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud marketplace syndication & SKU playbook

Rachel —

Thanks for pulling this together, very helpful. Quick notes inline:

- AWS: agree on three-tier, but recommend we add a single "BYOC/Private" plan mapping for Dedicated customers who prefer reserved capacity (this maps to Dedicated SKU in our billing). Also, can we add a field in the matrix for "support SLA" per SKU? AWS co-sell often pushes SLA requirements.

- Azure: I like the Growth consolidation for faster time-to-list and simpler procurement. But we should ensure our metering & metered billing descriptors match their marketplace schema (metering dimension names differ by cloud). Karthik, can your team validate the metering keys?

- GCP: agree on Starter+Enterprise approach. For APAC, GCP has earlier marketplace acceptance in SEA than AWS; maybe we can prioritize SG/HK listings if Sophie confirms.

Also: pricing margins will vary by cloud due to revenue share. We need high-level approval from Finance on list price floors before finalizing. Marissa, can you loop finance?

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@aws-partner.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud marketplace syndication & SKU playbook

Rachel / Jonas —

Appreciate the draft, looks straightforward. A few AWS-specific constraints and suggestions:

1) SKU naming: AWS prefers alphanumeric product codes for mapping to their billing catalog; you can keep human-friendly display names (Starter / Scale / Enterprise) but include an internal AWS product code column.

2) Region coverage: US/EU is fine for initial GA. For AUS/IN, we need proof of local data residency controls for some large accounts — list those as "restricted" in the matrix.

3) Co-sell: our commercial teams like to see a discrete "co-sell enablement pack" per SKU (one-pager, solution brief, 1-pager POC runbook). If Redwood owns these assets we can move faster.

4) Timeline: AWS marketplace ingestion typically takes 4-6 weeks given our validation process; listings with separate metering dimensions (e.g., tokens vs. seats) add extra review time.

I'll upload a sample product code template and our intake checklist to the shared Drive after lunch. Also copying Tom & Sophie to keep them in the loop.

-Maya
Maya Gupta
Partner Programs, AWS Marketplace

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud marketplace syndication & SKU playbook

Thanks Maya — useful detail. Quick synthesis and next steps so we have a single source of truth:

Decisions:
- AWS: list Starter/Scale/Enterprise + BYOC/Private mapping. Regions: US, EU (ga); AUS/IN in wave 2 but flagged as restricted for select accounts. Add product code column per AWS template.
- Azure: aggregate Starter+Scale into "Growth" + Enterprise. Regions: US, EU only for GA. Ensure metering dimension names match Azure schema.
- GCP: list Starter (trial tier) + Enterprise. Regions: US, EU-west. Prioritize SG/HK if Sophie confirms faster listing windows.

Owners & action items (owners in parens):
- Finalize SKU nomenclature and product codes (Jonas, Maya to provide template)
- Map metering dimensions per cloud and confirm with infra (Karthik)
- Pricing floor sign-off (Marissa -> Finance)
- Co-sell enablement assets: one-pager + POC runbook (Vanessa)
- Upload final matrix and intake assets to shared Drive (Rachel)

Timelines: aiming for AWS & Azure GA drafts in 6 weeks; GCP pilot concurrently but may lag. If partner intake checklists are posted, we'll slot them into the matrix and flag any blockers.

I'll consolidate feedback into v0.4 of the matrix and share a Drive link by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone for quick replies.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Marketplace Partnerships (acting)
Redwood Inference
